sentences.text:
2. MFA No.200407/2018 filed by appellants/claimants under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act,
1988 (for short 'the Act') seeking enhancement of compensation granted for the death of their son-Nagendra in a motor vehicles accident dated 30.03.2015
. While MFA No.200842/2017 filed by NEKRTC (for short 'Corporation') on the basis of quantum of compensation granted by the Tribunal.
3. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to by their rank before the Tribunal.
4. Petitioners are the parents of deceased- Nagendra.

It is the case of the petitioners that on 30.03.2015 at about 5:15 p.m. the deceased-Nagendra was proceeding towards his village Medak after getting Darshan of Lord Keshava, when he was near Gangarvalapalli cross on his motorcycle,
at that time, bus bearing Reg.No.KA-33/F-191 came in a high speed and in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the deceased and died on the spot.
The respondent is internal insurer of the vehicle, is liable to pay the compensation.
Hence, prayed to allow the petition.
5. Respondent appeared and filed written statement denying the age, occupation, income of the deceased and also that petitioners were dependent on him.
It is contended that the accident occurred only due to rash and negligent riding of the deceased not the driver of the bus.
It is submitted that there was contributory negligence by the deceased.
Hence, prays to dismiss the petition.
6. Based on these pleadings, the Tribunal framed necessary issues.
7. On behalf of the petitioners, petitioner No.1 is examined as P.W.1 and Exs.P1 to 16 got marked.
On behalf of respondent RW.1 is examined and got marked Ex.R1.

8. Vide the impugned judgment and award, the Tribunal has partly allowed the petition and quantified the compensation at Rs.9,31,000/- with interest at 6% per annum and directed respondent/corporation to pay the same.

9. The details of the compensation granted are as under:
 Sl. Head Amount awarded  No.
 1. Loss of dependency Rs.7,56,000/-
 2. Funeral and transportation Rs.25,000/-
 expenses  3. Towards loss of love and Rs.40,000/-
 affection  4. Loss of consortium Rs.1,00,000/-
 5. Loss of estate Rs.10,000/-
 Total Rs.9,31,000/-

sentences.text: During the course of argument, learned counsel for the petitioners submitted that the income taken at Rs.7,000/- p.m. is on the lower side.
It has not added any amount towards future prospects.
The compensation granted under other heads is also on the lower side and prays to allow the appeal.

11. On the other hand, learned counsel for respondent contended that the alleged accident took place due to negligence of deceased as he was riding his motorcycle in the middle of the road as per the spot map, this aspect of contributory negligence of the deceased was not considered by the Tribunal.
He further contended that deceased was bachelor and the Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.1,00,000/- towards loss of consortium, which is excessive.
Hence, the impugned judgment of the Tribunal needs to be modified.

12. Heard arguments and perused the records.
13.

Since the accident is of the year 2015, the income ought to have been taken at Rs.8,000/- p.m.
instead of Rs.7,000/- p.m.
The deceased was aged 22 years, the appropriate multiplier would be 18.

However, the Tribunal has not added any compensation towards loss of future prospects, as per Magma General Insurance Company Limited Vs. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram And Others1,
(Magma's case), 40% is required to be added towards loss of future prospects.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Company Limited Vs. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram And Others1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, the income is required to be taken at Rs.11,200/-.
Since deceased was bachelor, 50% is required to be deducted towards his personal and living expenses.

With these components, the compensation under the head loss of dependency is Rs.11,200 x 12 x 18 x 50% =
Rs.12,09,600/- (rounded off to Rs.12,10,000/-) as against Rs.7,56,000/- granted by the Tribunal.

14. As parents, petitioners are entitled for compensation in a sum of Rs.40,000/- each i.e.,
Rs.80,000/- under the head loss of consortium.
Similarly Rs.15,000/- each is awarded towards loss of estate and funeral expenses including transportation of dead body.

Thus, in all petitioners are entitled for total compensation in a sum of Rs.13,20,000/- as against Rs.09,31,000/- granted by the Tribunal with interest at 6% per annum as detailed below:

He further contended that the Tribunal has awarded exorbitant compensation towards loss of dependency and towards loss of consortium and same needs to be reduced and the judgment and award of the Tribunal needs to be modified.

17. To this extent, the impugned judgment and award of the Tribunal required to be modified and accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER (i) Both appeals are allowed in part.

(ii) Appellants/petitioners are entitled for  compensation in a sum of Rs.13,20,000/- as against Rs.9,31,000/-
granted by the Tribunal together with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.

(iii) Respondent/Corporation shall deposit the compensation amount within a period of six weeks from the date of this order together with interest at 6% p.a. (minus the compensation already paid/deposited).

(v) It is made clear that the interim award/compensation passed by this Court, if any, shall be deducted.
(vi) The amount deposited before this court by the respondent-Corporation, if any, is directed to be transmitted to the Tribunal.
